concerns.text: T024e selects 'first 20 datasets alphabetically' to comply with runtime constraints. Spec US-003 and FR-004 mandate the system MUST execute the pipeline for 'ALL available datasets' (or the full set if feasible) and only flag shortfalls. The task silently narrows the scope to 20 without an explicit 'staged' clause in the spec, violating the requirement to process the full dataset set for the correlation analysis (Constitution Principle VII).

T063 and T064 are marked as pending (`- [ ]`) and depend on artifacts (e.g., `generate_final_summary.py`) that are not yet implemented or defined in previous phases. The 'Dependencies & Execution Order' section lists Phase 8 as a prerequisite for 'Final sign-off', creating a circular dependency where the project cannot be signed off until the very tasks that are currently incomplete are finished. This violates the requirement for a complete, executable task list.

T015a is defined as the sole prerequisite for T031 (US-003) and the denominator for the Recovery Ratio. T019c (Sensitivity Analysis) is marked 'NON-BLOCKING'. However, T031's logic explicitly forbids using T019c for the denominator. The task list creates a high risk of implementation error where an engineer might accidentally use the aggregated sensitivity metrics (T019c) instead of the single-seed baseline (T015a) if the code comments are missed, potentially violating FR-001's requirement for a consistent, re-computed baseline.

T034 applies Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR) correction only to correlation p-values, while T035 performs a t-test. Spec SC-003 requires 'FDR correction applied for multiple features' but does not explicitly state whether the t-test (comparing a single mean against a constant) constitutes a 'family of tests' requiring correction alongside the correlations. The task list's separation creates ambiguity on whether the t-test p-value should also be FDR-corrected, potentially violating the statistical rigor required by FR-006.

T061 generates a `zero_variance_audit.log` to verify feature handling. Constitution Principle V (Versioning Discipline) requires that every artifact under the project carries a content hash and updates the `state/projects/...yaml` artifact hash map. The task description does not explicitly mandate that the `zero_variance_audit.log` itself be checksummed and recorded in the state map, risking a violation of Principle V where the audit log changes without updating the project state hash.
